Linde India acquires Airtech for ₹111.20 crore
sum: - Linde India acquires 100% stake in Airtech Cryogenic Gases
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Linde India acquired 100% of the share capital of Airtech Cryogenic Gases Private Limited for an estimated ₹111.20 crore. The deal, approved by the board on November 13, 2026, strengthens the company's position in the industrial and medical gases sector.

The acquisition involves a cash consideration and is subject to closing adjustments. Upon completion of conditions precedent, Airtech will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Linde India. The transaction does not require any governmental or regulatory approvals and is expected to be completed within 8 weeks.

Airtech Cryogenic Gases Private Limited operates in the manufacturing, sales, and distribution of industrial and medical cryogenic gases. The company maintains an Air Separation Unit at Dholka, Gujarat. It was incorporated on April 10, 2023.

The target company reported a turnover of ₹2,899.95 lakh for the 9 months of operation ending March 31, 2026. This represents a significant scale-up from the previous fiscal year, where turnover stood at ₹4.58 lakh. In the fiscal year ended March 31, 2024, the company recorded nil turnover, reflecting its recent incorporation.

Linde India stated that the acquisition aims to strengthen its core business, scale, and growth. The target entity’s business aligns with Linde India’s main line of operations. There are no related party transactions involved in this acquisition, and neither the promoter nor promoter group companies hold any interest in the target entity.

items.t: Linde (LIN) Stock May Look Fully Valued Following Strong Q3 Results
Is Linde (LIN) Reasonably Priced Given Its Earnings Strength?
sum: Linde has delivered strong returns in recent years, and with the stock last closing at US$526.55, the key question now is whether that price is supported by the company's earnings power. Investors have a lot of good news to work with, but the real focus is how much of that story is already embedded in the current valuation.
- Over the past 5 years, Linde has returned 70.2%, which puts real pressure on today's buyers to judge whether the earnings profile can justify paying up at current levels.

- Recent earnings updates point to steady EPS growth and an expanding project backlog, which can support expectations for future profit streams and therefore influence how much investors are willing to pay for each dollar of earnings.
- Your read on Linde is one view; the desks covering it have another. See what analysts think Linde's shares could be worth.
The issue now is whether Linde's current share price fairly reflects what its earnings record and outlook suggest the stock is worth.
If you are questioning whether Linde's earnings justify its price, you might want to apply the same earnings test across 32 high quality undervalued stocks.

P/E works well for Linde because investors clearly focus on the earnings line as the main driver of value. On this measure, the stock trades on roughly 34.5x earnings, compared with a Chemicals industry average near 23.8x and a broader peer group closer to 57.1x. That leaves Linde priced at a premium to the sector but below many large cap peers that investors treat as quality compounders.

sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Linde (LIN) is still working to repair its U.S. home care business, Lincare, a division management says has weighed on the company’s overall results. Management is restructuring the unit and reviewing its options, but the outlook for the fourth quarter of 2026 counts on no meaningful profit change from that work. The open question is how much earnings growth Linde stands to win back.

So far in 2026, Lincare has taken about 2 percentage points off Linde’s earnings per share growth, management said on its third-quarter 2026 call on October 29. Asked later on the call, the finance chief put the drag at about 1.5% to 2%. Management also said that removing that drag will support a return to double-digit EPS growth for the company. Elsewhere, margin gains in the gas segments were offset by declines in Engineering and Global Other, the segment Lincare now reports in.
Analysts asked about the restructuring on that call. Asked whether the Lincare savings would replace Linde’s usual productivity gains in 2027, management said they will come on top.

For the full year, management guides adjusted EPS growth of 8% to 9%, or 6% to 7% excluding currency. Management called this a more cautious view for the near term. For the fourth quarter alone, it guides growth of 5% to 7%, following 9% growth in the third quarter. The double-digit pace management links to fixing Lincare sits above this current guidance.
You are already paying for growth. Linde stock trades at 34.3 times its earnings over the last twelve months, against 22.3 for the S&P 500. The price appears to assume that growth holds up.

Linde booked a $425 million restructuring charge in the third quarter. Roughly half of it is severance, and most of the rest covers portfolio and asset actions at Lincare, where management is evaluating strategic alternatives. Management expects the severance part of the charge to pay back in cash in close to two years. The effect starts in the fourth quarter, with full benefits expected in the second half of next year.

Linde India's (NSE:LINDEINDIA) Shareholders Have More To Worry About Than Only Soft Earnings
sum: Despite Linde India Limited's (NSE:LINDEINDIA) recent earnings report having lackluster headline numbers, the market responded positively. Sometimes, shareholders are willing to ignore soft numbers with the hope that they will improve, but our analysis suggests this is unlikely for Linde India.

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

For the year to September 2026, Linde India had an accrual ratio of 0.26. We can therefore deduce that its free cash flow fell well short of covering its statutory profit. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of ₹6.8b despite its profit of ₹4.94b, mentioned above. Coming off the back of negative free cash flow last year, we imagine some shareholders might wonder if its cash burn of ₹6.8b, this year, indicates high risk.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Linde India didn't convert much of its profit to free cash flow in the last year, which some investors may consider rather suboptimal. Therefore, it seems possible to us that Linde India's true underlying earnings power is actually less than its statutory profit. But at least holders can take some solace from the 18% per annum growth in EPS for the last three.

sum: - Linde beat the quarter expectations and raised its full-year adjusted earnings view.
- Linde posted a quarterly profit beat recently and raised its full-year adjusted earnings outlook, helped by electronics, pricing and a large project backlog.

Linde plc (NASDAQ:LIN) Basic Materials Linde plc Ordinary Shares (NASDAQ:LIN) 515.25 USD -5.980 1.147% Last Updated at: 2026-11-06T21:00:00Z , the world's largest industrial gas supplier by revenue, posted quarterly results recently that beat the average analyst forecast and prompted the company to lift its outlook for the full year. The release therefore became one of the more widely shared earnings stories in the large-cap materials space that week. It remains relevant because the numbers contain a puzzle that readers keep raising: adjusted measures rose briskly while posted net income and posted earnings per share fell.

According to the company's release, sales grew by a set range, producing record quarterly sales. Underlying sales, which strip out currency and cost pass-through effects, rose notably, with pricing contributing most of that and volume adding the rest. Adjusted operating profit climbed by a similar order of magnitude to a substantial sum, and the adjusted operating margin held close to the high-twenties, a level that few industrial companies match. Adjusted earnings per share rose notably to a figure that topped the consensus estimate cited by TheFly, while revenue also exceeded expectations.

The most discussed oddity is the gap between measures. Posted net income dropped notably and posted diluted earnings per share fell notably. The company explains that adjusted figures exclude acquisition accounting effects tied to the long-ago Linde AG combination and charges associated with cost reduction programmes. Those items are real accounting costs, but they do not reflect the operating performance of the plants and distribution network in the same way. Skeptics argue that recurring adjustments can flatter results, and they note that cost reduction charges have appeared in several periods.
Regional detail shows a broad but uneven picture. The Americas posted the strongest margin, in the mid-thirties, and double-digit sales growth.

sum: Linde reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$9,404 million and net income of US$1,692 million, with basic EPS from continuing operations of US$3.67, alongside a US$1.60 per share quarterly dividend declared in October 2026.
The latest results show higher sales and net income for the first nine months of 2026 compared with the prior year, which hints at operating resilience despite quarterly earnings pressure.
We will look at how Linde's investment narrative aligns with higher year to date earnings but softer third quarter profitability.
Compare Linde's earnings and dividend profile with a curated 7 dividend fortresses that shares a similar focus on income and resilience.

Linde appeals to shareholders who buy into a long pipeline of gas projects in electronics, clean hydrogen, space and helium, supported by long term contracts and high capital intensity. The recent quarter shows that even with softer profitability, nine month earnings and sales remain solid, so the core project backlog and sale of gas model still look intact.

The most important near term catalyst is efficient conversion of that US$8.1b sale of gas backlog into on stream projects without further margin slippage. The biggest risk remains structural weakness in European industrial demand, combined with the drag from the U.S. homecare unit and a balance sheet that already carries meaningful debt.

The third quarter 2026 earnings release is the key update here. Sales of US$9,404 million and net income of US$1,692 million sit alongside nine month figures of US$27,474 million and US$5,477 million. That mix signals volume and pricing support for Linde while reminding you that net margin pressure can still creep in, particularly in weaker regions and legacy businesses.

Linde stock raises 2026 outlook after record third quarter
sum: Linde reported record third-quarter sales and adjusted earnings on Thursday, October 29, while raising its full-year 2026 adjusted earnings outlook. The industrial gases company said demand in electronics, chemicals and energy, and manufacturing supported the quarter. Its release was carried by Morningstar via Business Wire.

Sales reached 9.404 billion US dollars, an increase of 9 percent from the prior-year quarter. Underlying sales rose 5 percent, with price attainment contributing 3 percent and volumes 2 percent. Adjusted operating profit increased 8 percent to 2.763 billion US dollars, producing an adjusted operating margin of 29.4 percent.

Reported diluted EPS fell 11 percent to 3.66 US dollars because of purchase-accounting effects and cost-reduction and other charges. On an adjusted basis, EPS rose 9 percent to 4.59 US dollars, while adjusted net income increased 7 percent to 2.122 billion US dollars. Operating cash flow gained 8 percent to 3.169 billion US dollars, and free cash flow totaled 1.777 billion US dollars after capital spending.

Management raised the full-year adjusted EPS range to 17.82 to 17.92 US dollars from 17.70 to 17.90 US dollars, assuming a 2 percent favorable currency effect. The company expects fourth-quarter adjusted EPS of 4.40 to 4.50 US dollars, representing growth of 5 to 7 percent from the year-earlier quarter. Planned 2026 capital spending remains between 5.5 billion and 6.0 billion US dollars.

Electronics sales grew 15 percent year over year, according to Reuters, published by Fidelity. The report linked the strongest end-market performance to demand for gases used in semiconductor manufacturing as producers expand capacity for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing chips.

Chief Executive Officer Sanjiv Lamba said proposal activity remained robust, particularly in electronics, and that Linde expected continued backlog growth. The company reported a project backlog of 11 billion US dollars and said it was focusing on productivity, operational execution, and disciplined capital deployment.

sum: Jim Cramer urged investors to buy shares of industrial gas giant Linde on Friday's dip, calling the company "one of the greatest stories of our time" during a volatile week for technology and industrial stocks.

Speaking on the CNBC Investing Club's "Morning Meeting," Cramer and portfolio director Jeff Marks recommended that new club members initiate a position in Linde (LIN) as shares fell nearly 6% despite a modest earnings beat. The decline came amid broader market crosscurrents, with bond yields surging to their highest levels since January 2025 and oil prices jumping after Iran said it attacked tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.
"This is an odd market," Cramer said, pointing to the 10-year Treasury yield's climb as the primary reason early morning stock gains evaporated.

Linde's electronics division delivered standout performance, posting 18% year-over-year growth and securing a major contract with Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM). However, investor sentiment soured over weakness in the company's home health care business. Management said it is evaluating strategic options for that unit, a proactive approach Marks praised.
"That's exactly what investors like to hear when a unit isn't generating the best results," Marks said.
Cramer's bullish call on Linde came against a backdrop of dramatic divergence in mega-cap technology earnings.

Amazon (AMZN) shares soared more than 14% following what the CNBC Investing Club characterized as a fantastic quarter. The cloud computing and e-commerce leader raised its capital expenditure guidance but eased investor concerns by detailing how it plans to monetize its artificial intelligence investments. Cramer urged investors to listen to CEO Andy Jassy's earnings call breakdown of the company's data center strategy.
